brief: Design an interface for "Memory Pressure Cooking" where users preserve fleeting thoughts before they evaporate by dragging ephemeral text fragments into mason jars that seal with satisfying pneumatic

dominant_strengths: Warm pantry-shelf palette and glass jar rendering create strong visceral metaphor that reinforces the preservation concept
Italic serif hint text paired with framed thought fragment establishes a contemplative, literary tone that fits ephemerality
Subtle glow within filled jars (purple, amber) gives memories a perceived 'essence' without overdesigning
dominant_weaknesses: Affordance for dragging is unclear: jar lids look static and identical, no visible drop zone or pneumatic seal feedback in still frame
Tiny labels inside jars are low-contrast and cramped against the glass gradient, hurting legibility of the core content
Two shelf rows are visually identical with no hierarchy, categorization, or sense of fill progression to motivate behavior
fix_priorities: Add explicit drop-target affordance on hover (lid lift, glow ring) and a visible seal animation cue in static state
Increase label contrast and typographic scale inside jars; consider a small engraved-tag treatment instead of floating text
Differentiate shelves by category, time, or fullness so the wall tells a story rather than reading as a uniform grid
Show the evaporation timer on the floating fragment itself so urgency is felt, not just stated in the subtitle
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the jar metaphor, but behavioral clarity lags because interaction targets and feedback are under-signaled.
rationale.intent_fit: It captures the poetic preservation metaphor convincingly, yet the 'pressure' and 'pneumatic seal' urgency from the brief is barely expressed in the static composition.
